A tsunami crosses an ocean at the speed of a jet and rises into a wall of water near shore. Here is the science.

#shorts #science #tsunami #ocean #nature

sahneler.metin: A tsunami is a wall of ocean moving faster than you can run.
It can race across the sea as fast as a jet.
Yet in deep water, a boat wouldn't even feel it pass.
So what gives it that power?
An earthquake jerks the seafloor up, shoving huge volumes of water.
Near shore it slows and piles up into a towering wall.
The sea often pulls back first, exposing the seabed.
If the sea retreats, run for high ground.

vaka.yanilgi: A tsunami isn't a giant curling surf wave — it behaves more like a fast-rising tide that doesn't stop.
